description: "A two-hour, hands-on introduction to genotype quality control, PCA, GWASpoly, and genomic selection in BIGapp."

BIGapp is a free R Shiny application for processing and analyzing low- to mid-density genotype data in diploid and polyploid species. This workshop uses its graphical interface, so no R or command-line experience is required.

::: {.callout-important}
## Install BIGapp before the workshop

The hands-on exercises run in a local BIGapp installation. The [public online BIGapp](https://big-demo.shinyapps.io/bigapp-main/) is a view-only preview for becoming familiar with the interface. Do not use the shared preview to run the workshop data or analyses.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## About this adaptation

These maintained materials are adapted from the original [Introduction to BIGapp for Plant Breeding workshop](https://alex-sandercock.github.io/biotools/workshops/bigapp-2025/). Interface labels and checkpoints have been updated for the official BIGapp main release.
:::

## Who this is for

This workshop is designed for students, researchers, and breeders who want to use genomic data without first learning a programming language. Familiarity with plant breeding is helpful, but prior experience with R, VCF files, or bioinformatics is not required.

## What you will learn

By the end of the guided modules, you will be able to:

1. Explain what SNP genotypes and allele dosage represent.
2. Filter low-depth genotype cells, markers, and samples with adjustable criteria.
3. Use PCA to inspect population structure and possible outliers.
4. Run GWASpoly and interpret its BIC, Manhattan, QQ, and LD-window results.
5. Describe how cross-validation supports genomic prediction decisions.

## What you need

- R 4.4.0 or later and a local BIGapp installation
- A current web browser with JavaScript enabled
- Internet access during setup to install R packages
- The three local files described in the [dataset guide](dataset-guide.qmd)
- Enough free disk space for BIGapp, its R-package dependencies, the workshop files, and saved results

::: {.callout-important}
## Download the files before the session

- [Genotype VCF, compressed](data/atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity.vcf.gz){download="atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity.vcf.gz"}
- [Phenotypes and sample metadata CSV](data/atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity_phenotypes.csv){download="atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity_phenotypes.csv"}
- [SNP-information CSV](data/atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity_snp_info.csv){download="atlantic_giant_pumpkin_diversity_snp_info.csv"}
:::

## The workflow

The guided analysis follows one continuous sequence:

1. Install BIGapp, start it locally, and check the example files.
2. Filter the VCF with dataset-specific example thresholds.
3. Inspect genetic structure with PCA.
4. Test the simulated fruit-weight trait with GWASpoly.
5. Optionally estimate predictive ability and generate genomic predictions.

Each module includes written steps and a collapsible answer. The animations are supplementary, so you can complete every exercise without relying on them.

## Help and reporting problems

For software problems, unexpected results, or feature requests, [open an issue in the BIGapp repository](https://github.com/Breeding-Insight/BIGapp/issues). Include the BIGapp version or public-demo URL, the browser and operating system, the step that failed, and the complete error message. Do not attach private genotype or phenotype files to a public issue.
